title: How should screw-bone contact be modelled in the pull-out solver?
context: Pull-out force depends heavily on how thread flanks engage the foam. The current grid-based contact smears the interface over one cell, which may underpredict peak force on fine threads.

options.name: Keep grid contact, refine locally
options.summary: Leave the contact method alone and add a finer grid band around the screw.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='20' y='20' width='280' height='140' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.12'/><g stroke='currentColor' stroke-opacity='0.25'><path d='M20 60H300M20 100H300M20 140H300M80 20V160M140 20V160M200 20V160M260 20V160'/></g><rect x='125' y='20' width='70' height='140' fill='var(--accent)' fill-opacity='0.25'/><g stroke='var(--accent)' stroke-opacity='0.6'><path d='M125 40H195M125 60H195M125 80H195M125 100H195M125 120H195M125 140H195M140 20V160M160 20V160M180 20V160'/></g><path d='M150 20V160M170 20V160' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='3'/><text x='160' y='175' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>finer band at screw</text></svg>
cons: Run time grows with band size
Still smears the interface, just less
assumptions: Under-prediction comes mainly from grid resolution, not the contact rule itself
risks: Band size needed for convergence may make runs too slow to compare many designs

estimates.basis: band roughly doubles the active cells near the screw

options.name: Explicit thread surface
options.summary: Represent the thread as a rigid surface and resolve contact against it directly.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='20' y='20' width='280' height='140' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.12'/><path d='M160 20 L180 35 L160 50 L180 65 L160 80 L180 95 L160 110 L180 125 L160 140 L180 155' fill='none' stroke='var(--accent)' stroke-width='3'/><g fill='currentColor' fill-opacity='0.45'><circle cx='190' cy='35' r='3'/><circle cx='190' cy='65' r='3'/><circle cx='190' cy='95' r='3'/><circle cx='190' cy='125' r='3'/><circle cx='150' cy='50' r='3'/><circle cx='150' cy='80' r='3'/><circle cx='150' cy='110' r='3'/><circle cx='150' cy='140' r='3'/></g><text x='230' y='60' font-size='12' fill='currentColor'>sharp flank</text><text x='230' y='76' font-size='12' fill='currentColor'>contact</text></svg>
pros: Sensitivity to thread pitch becomes visible
cons: New contact code on the GPU
assumptions: Thread geometry can be imported cleanly as a rigid surface
Foam crush behavior near the flank is captured by the existing material model
risks: New GPU contact code may be unstable at large penetrations

estimates.basis: contact check is per particle near the surface only
new contact pass plus a recalibration round

options.name: Empirical correction factor
options.summary: Keep the solver and multiply peak force by a factor fitted from test data per thread family.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><path d='M40 150H290M40 150V25' stroke='currentColor' stroke-opacity='0.6'/><path d='M40 150 C100 120 140 80 180 75 S250 110 280 130' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-opacity='0.5' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><path d='M40 150 C100 105 140 50 180 42 S250 95 280 118' fill='none' stroke='var(--accent)' stroke-width='3'/><text x='60' y='40' font-size='12' fill='currentColor'>force</text><text x='240' y='168' font-size='12' fill='currentColor'>pull distance</text><text x='186' y='34' font-size='12' fill='var(--accent)'>scaled</text></svg>
cons: Breaks on thread designs outside the fitted set
assumptions: Thread designs users test stay close to the fitted set
risks: A factor fitted on one foam grade may not transfer to another

criteria.name: Calibration effort
criteria.note: B needs a fresh round against held-back tests.

recommendation: Thread pitch is what users are comparing, and only an explicit surface resolves it. Worth confirming against two or three held-back tests before trusting it.

evidence.claim: Grid-based contact in material point methods spreads the interface across about one cell, which softens sharp features.
Pull-out strength in foam is sensitive to thread pitch and flank angle.
A correction factor is unlikely to survive large changes in thread form, since it cannot respond to geometry.

change_mind: If refining the grid band alone closes most of the gap to held-back tests, A wins on effort.
